correctness.rationale: The Choi partial-transpose matrix consists of positive one-dimensional diagonal sectors and explicit 2x2 sectors, giving necessity if and only if s/(1-s) does not exceed every sqrt(p_i p_j). The independent cubic-phase finite product-projector sum reconstructs exactly the Choi offdiagonal sector; its residue is diagonal and coefficientwise nonnegative under precisely those inequalities, giving all-dimensional sufficiency. Trace and normalization are explicit; Lindblad jumps L_ij=sqrt(gamma p_i)|i><j| reproduce the reset generator and s=exp(-gamma t). At s=0 and at the equality boundary the product decomposition still holds. Direct NumPy checks on full package script corroborate the identities in dimensions 3 to 5, not replacing their proofs.

originality.rationale: The proven full-rank, >=3-eigenvalue and d>=3 exact threshold and explicit finite phase-twirled separable decomposition are not supplied by the comparison texts: [1] is a general criterion, [2] covers ordinary unital depolarization and estimates for general semigroups, [3] covers the d=2 Bell-mixing setting, and [4] defines a closely related family whose stationary state has at most two distinct eigenvalues. None of the matched published records states a stronger result implying the present at-least-three-eigenvalue theorem. The later portions of [4] were not fully accessible, so an unseen general lemma remains a stated residual risk rather than being declared absent.

value.rationale: The first time a thermal quantum reset channel necessarily destroys entanglement with any ancilla is an operational memory lifetime. Existing general eventual-EB theorems and the isotropic benchmark do not determine it for genuine multi-level anisotropic stationary spectra. This infinite family is classified by the two smallest populations, with a constructive PPT-to-separable result valid despite PPT generally being insufficient in dimensions >=3. The exact two-smallest-level dependence identifies which thermal excitation tail controls complete entanglement loss; neither a chosen parameter slice nor a bare numerical threshold.
